oneLine: Strong U.S. economic data sent bond yields to 19-year highs on September 23, triggering profit-taking in Bitcoin (down 2.1%) and Ethereum (down 2.5%) as investors rotated capital into bonds.
caveman: On September 23, economists released news that America's job market and business activity were growing faster than expected. Normally crypto traders like good economic news, but this time it worked against them. Here's why: when the economy is strong, the government can offer higher interest rates on bonds—the super-safe investment that big money uses. The rate on 10-year U.S. bonds jumped to its highest level since 2007. So money managers thought: 'Why take the risk of owning Bitcoin and Ethereum when I can buy bonds and get really good interest?' They started selling crypto and buying bonds. That's why Bitcoin dropped about 2% and Ethereum dropped about 2.5% during the day. The stock market also fell. But something interesting happened: even though prices were dropping, huge investment funds kept buying Bitcoin—they put in about $1.7 billion over two days. So the day felt mixed: prices falling, but smart money still buying.
priceVolumeSummary: All five major exchanges (Binance, OKX, Bybit, Bitget, Gate) reported nearly identical prices for both Bitcoin and Ethereum throughout the day, showing strong agreement across venues. Binance led trading volume, with $17.8 billion in BTC volume and $11.9 billion in ETH volume, followed by OKX.
positioningSummary: Historical funding rates and open-interest data are unavailable for this date. However, spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted approximately $1.7 billion in net inflows over September 22–23 despite the price decline, suggesting institutional traders remained confident in the underlying assets even as short-term traders took profits on the bond-yield shock.

movers.explanation: Down 2.1% as the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield surged over 13 basis points to 5.1% (highest since 2007) following upbeat S&P Global economic data showing business activity, manufacturing, and employment all accelerating at their fastest pace in years. Investors rotated out of risky assets like crypto into higher-yielding bonds.

Down 2.5%, tracking Bitcoin in a broad risk-off rotation driven by rising bond yields. Spot Ethereum ETFs still recorded $162.2 million in net inflows, showing institutional support despite the price pullback.

topThree.headline: U.S. bond yields spike to 19-year highs on strong economic data, triggering crypto selloff
topThree.what: The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield jumped over 13 basis points to 5.1%, the highest since 2007, after S&P Global reported business activity accelerating at its fastest pace since July 2021, with employment rising at its fastest pace since 2022. The surge in bond yields triggered a broad risk-off rotation, with capital flowing out of Bitcoin, Ethereum, and risky stocks into safer bonds. The Nasdaq fell 1.1% and the S&P 500 fell 0.75%.

Traditional markets.headline: Treasury yields surge to 19-year highs amid robust economic data and rising oil prices
Traditional markets.what: The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.1%, the highest since 2007. S&P Global data showed private-sector business activity expanding at its fastest pace since July 2021, with both manufacturing and services sectors accelerating and employment rising at its fastest pace since 2022. Oil prices also jumped above $103 per barrel, amplifying the yield-driven rotation out of risky assets.

Institutional flows and ETFs.headline: Spot Bitcoin ETFs pull in $1.7 billion over two days despite price decline
Institutional flows and ETFs.what: Spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted approximately $715 million on September 22 and significant additional inflows on September 23, for a two-day total exceeding $1.7 billion—the strongest two-day performance in over a year. BlackRock's IBIT remained the largest U.S. spot Bitcoin fund with $67.9 billion in assets. Ethereum spot ETFs posted $162.2 million in net inflows with BlackRock's ETHA leading at $88.1 million.

etfFlows.summary: Bitcoin spot ETFs attracted approximately $1.7 billion over two days (best haul in over a year), with roughly $715 million on September 22. Ethereum spot ETFs posted $162.2 million in net inflows on the same period, led by BlackRock's ETHA with $88.1 million. Both showed strong institutional demand despite crypto prices falling.

glossary.definition: The annual percentage of interest a bond investor receives. When bond yields rise, bonds become more attractive than other investments like crypto, often triggering capital rotation.
The interest traders with long positions pay to traders with short positions in perpetual futures contracts. It reflects whether the market sentiment is more bullish or bearish.
The proportion of traders betting the price will go up (long) versus traders betting it will go down (short). A higher ratio means more bullish sentiment in the market.
The reference price used to calculate profits and losses on perpetual futures, often derived from spot prices to prevent price manipulation.
The total number of unfinished futures or options contracts held by traders at any moment. Higher open interest typically indicates more conviction about a price direction.

How much the total number of open contracts increased or decreased over a time period. Growing open interest often means new money entering the market, while shrinking open interest means traders are closing positions.
When traders close winning positions and sell, locking in gains. Large waves of profit-taking can push prices lower even when sentiment remains positive.
When investors move money from riskier investments (like crypto and tech stocks) into safer, more stable ones (like government bonds) due to market uncertainty or changing economic conditions.
The total amount of an asset traded on an exchange over a time period, measured in dollars or coins. Higher volume typically means more liquidity and stronger trader interest.
